headline: 30 Years of Work Protects 25 Million Hectares Across Yellowstone to Yukon
meta_description: The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative celebrates three decades of protecting vast landscapes and reducing wildlife deaths through innovative crossin…
summary_short: After 30 years, a major conservation effort has protected 25 million hectares and built over 200 wildlife crossings, dramatically cutting vehicle collisions.
body:
After three decades of dedicated work, the Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative has protected roughly 25 million hectares across one of North America's most vital ecosystems.

The scale of this achievement becomes clear in a single figure: more than 200 wildlife crossings have been built across the region. These structures—overpasses, underpasses, and passage ways—serve a concrete purpose that saves lives. By giving animals safe routes across highways and developed areas, the initiative has measurably reduced wildlife-vehicle collisions that once claimed countless elk, deer, bears, and other species annually.

The project represents a shift in how conservation works on the ground: not through fences that divide, but through infrastructure that connects. Protecting a landscape means little if the animals living there cannot move freely to find food, mates, and new territory. Over three decades, this initiative has learned that lesson well, turning habitat protection and smart engineering into a working partnership between humans and wildlife.
quick_facts: 30 years of conservation work across Yellowstone to Yukon region
